title: No challenge: the server answers 200 without a token
describes: A token-less request is accepted, so there is no 401 and no WWW-Authenticate to discover from.

title: No protected resource metadata
describes: The well-known metadata URL answers 404 (the 401 challenge still points at it).

title: Metadata names a different resource
describes: The protected resource metadata resource value is not the MCP endpoint URL it was fetched for.

title: Authorization server issuer mismatch
describes: The authorization server metadata issuer carries a trailing slash that the protected resource metadata does not (not identical, RFC 8414 section 3.3).

title: Empty first auth-param in WWW-Authenticate
describes: The challenge is 'Bearer , resource_metadata=...' with a comma straight after the scheme.

title: resource_metadata uses http
describes: The 401 challenge advertises a plain-http metadata URL.

title: No scope hint in the 401 challenge
describes: The 401 challenge has resource_metadata but no scope parameter.

title: resource parameter ignored
describes: Tokens get a default audience and an unknown resource is accepted.

title: No iss in authorization responses
describes: Issuer identification is neither advertised nor returned.

title: Wrong 403 shape
describes: Insufficient scope answers a bare 403 with no error or scope in the challenge.

title: Open dynamic registration without limits
describes: Anonymous registration accepts any redirect URI and is never throttled.

title: Stale metadata
describes: Metadata is cacheable for a year and advertises an authorization endpoint that now answers 404.

title: Audience not validated
describes: The MCP endpoint accepts a token minted for another resource.

title: Gateway answers metadata for any path
describes: Protected resource metadata is returned for paths that do not exist.

title: No dynamic registration (CIMD only)
describes: registration_endpoint is not published. Not a defect: shown in the DCR versus CIMD comparison.
